title: Broken icon names render a sparkle glyph across 24 files — including beside the red error message in Correct Info and on the Tasks nav item
surface: Correct Info error box; left nav Tasks row; onboarding wizard success ticks; task board; notification list; and 18 other files
whatYouSee: A correction fails and the red error box shows a decorative sparkle next to the failure text. In the left nav, Tasks has a sparkle where every other item has a real icon. The onboarding wizard's completion ticks, the notification list's success marks and the task board's empty state are all sparkles too.
whyItsWrong: The shared icon component looks names up in the icon library's name map and quietly falls back to a sparkle for anything unknown. The installed library version (1.21.0) renamed a batch of icons and its name map contains only the new canonical names — the old names survive as module exports but are absent from the map the component uses. So every call site still using an old name renders a sparkle: 37 of them across 24 files. A cheerful sparkle attached to an error message, and an indistinguishable sparkle where a completion tick belongs, are the worst possible substitutions.
evidence: node_modules/lucide-react 1.21.0 — the exported icons map has 1737 keys and contains none of AlertCircle, AlertTriangle, CheckCircle, CheckCircle2, CheckSquare, Loader2, BarChart2, Wand2
src/components/correct-info-modal.tsx:120 — name="AlertCircle" beside the error text
src/components/tasks-board.tsx:624 — name="CheckSquare" in the empty state
fix: Rename at all 37 call sites (24 files, findable with a grep for the eight dead names): AlertCircle→CircleAlert, AlertTriangle→TriangleAlert, CheckCircle and CheckCircle2→CircleCheck, CheckSquare→SquareCheck, Loader2→LoaderCircle, BarChart2→ChartNoAxesColumn, Wand2→WandSparkles. Then make the fallback in src/components/icon.tsx:10 loud in development (console.warn when a name misses) so the next library rename cannot fail silently.

title: Clicking a task notification drops you on a board tab that does not contain that task
surface: Notifications bell → any "Pending tasks" or "Ready for review" row → Workspace
whatYouSee: The notification row has an arrow implying it takes you to the task. It goes to the board with no task identity, and the board always opens on the "Automated" tab. If the item you clicked is one of yours, you land on a tab that does not contain it — nothing on screen is the thing you just clicked.
whyItsWrong: The click-through target is wrong for a whole class of notifications, so the bell reads as broken — and it is worst for exactly the items the bell exists to chase, the ones the client has to do themselves.
fix: Link to `/tasks?task=<id>` from TaskAlertRow (src/components/notification-bell.tsx:286) and in TasksBoard (src/components/tasks-board.tsx:430) read that param with useSearchParams to (a) set activeTab from inferOwner of the matching task (helper at line 65) instead of the hardcoded "karos" default at line 439, and (b) set selectedTaskId so TaskTicketModal opens on mount. Cheap interim: derive the tab in the notification row and link to `/tasks?tab=client`, with TasksBoard honouring a tab param, so the person at least lands where the card is.

title: Task-creating actions never hand you off to the board where the tasks landed
surface: AI Copilot panel → the quick-add task box, the War Room completion state, and Content Dispatch
whatYouSee: Type a task and press Add: a small green pill says "AI-managed task added" and that is the end of it. Finish a War Room run: a green bar says "Consensus reached - 7 tasks locked into your map", then the window closes itself. Run a Content Dispatch: the assistant's closing line is prose along the lines of "Created 5 tasks in your task board." In all three cases there is nothing to click, and you may be sitting on the dashboard, the assets page or a document, none of which show tasks.
whyItsWrong: The panel is pinned to every workspace page, so it creates work from contexts that never show the result. None of the three components involved contain a single link. The quick-add is the worst of the three: the description is rewritten by a model and the owner is chosen for you, so the card that exists may not carry the words the client typed — and the confirmation shows neither the resulting title nor a way to look at it.
evidence: src/components/chatbot-widget.tsx:220-226 — success feedback is a static label, taskId is discarded
src/components/chatbot-widget.tsx:277-292 — the confirmation pill: icon + message only
src/lib/actions/task-actions.ts:346-355 — Haiku rewrites title/description and picks the owner
src/lib/actions/task-actions.ts:382-397 — createClientTask returns the id; the action returns taskId and owner but not the title
src/app/api/clients/[id]/chat/route.ts:610 — the "Created N tasks in your task board" string the model paraphrases
grep for Link|href in chatbot-widget.tsx, strategy-war-room.tsx, copilot-dock.tsx — zero matches
fix: Return the generated title from ingestCustomUserTaskAction (src/lib/actions/task-actions.ts:311 return type and line 397 — it already returns taskId and owner, add `title: parsed.title`). Then in src/components/chatbot-widget.tsx:277-292 render the confirmation as `Added "<title>"` plus a next/link to /tasks. Apply the identical change to the duplicate bar at src/components/quick-add-task-bar.tsx:33-41 for consistency (there the board is already on screen, so a link is optional). Add a "View task map" link to the War Room done footer at src/components/strategy-war-room.tsx:195-200 and remove the 1.6s auto-close at line 142 so the link is reachable. A ?task=<id> deep link is not supported today — src/app/(app)/tasks/page.tsx reads no searchParams — so link to /tasks unless you also add that.

title: The client's Archive is every deliverable they have ever received in one wall, with no filter, search, collapse or paging
whatYouSee: An agent name, then every tile that agent has ever produced, then the next agent, and so on. A client on three posts a week for a year sees roughly 150 tiles in one continuous scroll. There is no status filter, no date range, no search box, no way to fold up an agent group, and no show-more — while staff looking at the same deliverables get a status dropdown and a channel dropdown.
whyItsWrong: The client view maps every group and every item with no limit and no controls. The audience with the least context gets the least navigable surface. It also compounds the first finding: with no filter and no address state, nothing in the portal can send a client to "my drafts".
fix: Give ArchiveView the same control bar AssetsView has: add `status`, `agent` and a text `search` over `asset.title`, rendered in the identical `flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface-2 p-2` strip from src/components/assets-view.tsx:69-91, and seed `status` from the URL so finding 1's deep link can target drafts. Cap each agent group at 12 tiles behind a "Show all N" button reusing the collapse pattern at src/components/seo-geo/gap-list.tsx:143-152, and make the group heading at archive-view.tsx:77-81 a button that folds its grid.

title: The resume a client uploads is never read — but the UI says it powers their voice
surface: Account settings /settings — Profile tab, "Resume / CV" card (and the same uploader in the onboarding wizard)
whatYouSee: A drag-and-drop uploader captioned "Used to write LinkedIn advocacy content in your authentic voice", and once uploaded, "Powers your LinkedIn advocacy voice". The user uploads their CV and reasonably expects the agent to write like them. It does not.
whyItsWrong: The file's contents never reach a model. The upload endpoint stores the file and mirrors only its web address onto the employee seat; the advocacy prompt then pastes that address in as a bare line of text, and the generation call is issued with a prompt and no tools, so the model has no way to open or read it. The field the prompt actually uses to shape the voice is a raw-text background field, which no screen in the product ever fills in. The upload therefore does nothing except add an unusable link to a prompt.
evidence: src/components/settings-form.tsx:188 — "Used to write LinkedIn advocacy content in your authentic voice."
src/app/api/users/resume/route.ts:42 — stores resumeUrl on the user; line 44 mirrors only the URL onto the seat
src/lib/execution-engine.ts:372 — resumeText is sourced from seat.backgroundContext, not from the uploaded file
src/lib/actions/seat-actions.ts:104 — backgroundContext is only ever written from an action input no UI supplies (grep: no caller passes it)
src/lib/ai/prompts/proactive-assistant.ts:636 — the fallback branch: "Background/resume reference on file: {url}"
src/lib/execution-engine.ts:397 — generateText called with a prompt and no tools, so the URL cannot be fetched
fix: Extract text at upload time: in src/app/api/users/resume/route.ts, after uploadBytes at line 40, parse the PDF/DOCX/TXT to plain text and write it to the seat's `backgroundContext` via the existing updateEmployeeSeat call at line 44 (alongside resumeUrl) — that is the field src/lib/ai/prompts/proactive-assistant.ts:634 actually reads, mapped at src/lib/execution-engine.ts:372. Until that ships, change both captions (src/components/settings-form.tsx:188 and src/components/resume-uploader.tsx:88) to something true — "Stored for your Karos team" — and drop the dead URL branch at proactive-assistant.ts:635-636 so the model is not fed a link it cannot open (src/lib/__tests__/artifact-prompt.test.ts:49 asserts on that branch and will need updating).

title: The staff notification bell can never show a review or a task
whatYouSee: As an admin or employee the bell only ever lists meeting action items assigned to you. "Ready for review" and "Pending tasks" never appear no matter how full the review queue is, the panel says "All caught up!" when you have no meeting items, and the footer always offers "View all meetings" instead of the task board.
whyItsWrong: The workspace layout hands the bell empty lists for reviews and tasks unless the viewer is a client user, so two of its three feeds are structurally unreachable for the people who actually run the agency — and the empty state then asserts nothing needs attention while drafts sit in review.
fix: In src/app/(app)/layout.tsx populate both feeds for staff before rendering AppHeader (line 150): scope with listClients() for admins and listClients({ employeeId: user.uid }) for employees, then aggregate — listClientTasks already takes an optional clientId (src/lib/data.ts:1664-1670), so one cross-client call with a status filter works today, and the annotate-with-client-name pattern to copy is in src/app/(app)/tasks/tasks-body.tsx:92-104. listReviewJobs (src/lib/data.ts:1641) takes a single clientId, so either add an ids variant or map over the scoped clients. Cap the lists and show the client name on each row (ClientTask carries clientId).

title: When generation is running or has failed, the Documents group tells the client the wrong story — and "our team has been notified" is not true
surface: Documents nav group empty state (client portal rail) plus the workspace banner shown after a failed run
whatYouSee: A client who finished onboarding half an hour ago sees, under Documents, that their brand and strategy documents will appear once onboarding completes — implying they still have setup to do. If the run failed, that same line persists, alongside a banner saying we hit a snag and our team has been notified and is on it.
whyItsWrong: The documents list already receives the flag telling it a generation cycle is in flight, but only uses it to disable the admin Regenerate button — the empty state never mentions that generation is running, and never distinguishes running from failed from not-started. And nothing is notified: releasing the processing lock only writes an error string onto the client record. No email, no activity entry, no staff notification. The only reader of that field is the banner itself, which a staff member sees solely by opening that one client's dashboard or settings page. The reassurance is copy over a missing code path.
evidence: src/components/client-documents.tsx:749 — isAiProcessing used only to disable Regenerate
src/components/ai-processing-banner.tsx:40-41 — "Our team has been notified and is on it"
src/lib/data.ts:281-290 — releaseAiProcessingLock writes only the aiProcessingError field
src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/page.tsx:84 and src/app/(app)/clients/[id]/settings/page.tsx:96 — the only staff-visible readers of that field
fix: Two parts. (1) In src/components/client-documents.tsx:764, branch the empty state on state the component already has: isAiProcessing → "Karos Agents are writing your documents now — this takes a few minutes."; otherwise the existing onboarding line. Pass the client's aiProcessingError down (both mount points, src/components/sidebar.tsx:385 and src/components/client-rail.tsx:138, already hold the client record) for a third branch: "Generation stopped early. Your Karos team is on it." (2) Make the reassurance true: in the failure path of releaseAiProcessingLock (src/lib/data.ts:281) — or at each of its callers, which already have the failure string — write a logActivity entry and notify the assigned staff via the existing Resend mailer, or surface an error badge on the /clients list.

title: X drafts are titled with lab-internal vocabulary — clients read "Avenue 3 · News-reaction (live)" (and LinkedIn drafts read "Post 2 · POV thread")
surface: Assets / Workspace archive → X and LinkedIn drafts batch cards (asset detail and archive)
whatYouSee: Each draft block is headed by whatever the agent wrote in its own document: "Avenue 1 · Build-in-public", "Avenue 3 · News-reaction (live)", "Avenue 4 · Quote-comment". On the LinkedIn reader the same pattern appears as "Post 1 · knowledge/explainer", "Post 2 · POV thread".
whyItsWrong: The heading text is passed through verbatim from the agent's deliverable into the card title. "Avenue", the lane slugs, and the "(live)" freshness flag are production vocabulary from the agent contract, not language a client uses — nobody outside the lab knows what an Avenue or a POV single is. This is raw model-authored copy rendered straight to a client, which is exactly what the house copy rule forbids, and it is the first thing a client reads on every draft.
fix: Humanize at the render boundary, not in the parsers (the raw string is also used as the draftRef sent to the feedback actions — x-drafts-review.tsx:77 and li-drafts-review.tsx:99 — so those must keep the original text). Add a shared helper, e.g. src/lib/draft-lane-label.ts, exporting `laneLabel(heading: string): string` that strips a leading "Avenue N · " / "Post N · " / "Draft N · " prefix, looks the remainder up case-insensitively in a map (build-in-public → "Building in public", knowledge/explainer → "Explainer", news-reaction → "Reacting to the news", quote-comment → "Quote reply", reply → "Reply", pov single → "Your point of view", pov thread → "Your point of view (thread)") and sentence-cases anything unmapped. Then use it at src/components/x-drafts-review.tsx:137 (`{laneLabel(draft.avenue)}`) and src/components/li-drafts-review.tsx:153 (`{laneLabel(draft.lane)}`). Reddit needs no change — src/components/reddit-drafts-review.tsx:220 already prefers the real thread title and only falls back to the internal formula name.

title: Client-facing strings use a spaced hyphen where the rest of the UI uses an em dash — including the "drafts only, we never post" promise on all three agent pages
surface: X / LinkedIn / Reddit agent pages and drafts readers, copilot dock, processing banner, onboarding (portal-wide)
whatYouSee: "Drafts only - a person always posts." · "Drafts only - we never post to Reddit, you post the reply yourself." · "Sent - it feeds the next run." · "Locked - a workspace build is already running" · "Your final version - the wording you will actually post." · "Logged - the reason tunes r/SaaS" · "Let's get your workspace set up - it only takes a minute."
whyItsWrong: The same product uses em dashes correctly in hundreds of other strings, so punctuation visibly changes voice between adjacent screens. A spaced hyphen reads as a typo or a stray minus sign rather than a clause break, and it lands in the highest-trust copy in the product: the "we never post for you" promise on all three agent pages.
fix: Hand-replace " - " with " — " in user-visible strings only. Highest value first: the three agent page descriptions (x-agent/page.tsx:32, linkedin-agent/page.tsx:37, reddit-agent/page.tsx:35), then the intake and drafts readers (x-agent-intake.tsx has 11 hits, linkedin-agent-intake.tsx 10, reddit-drafts-review.tsx 8, li-drafts-review.tsx 3, reddit-agent-intake.tsx 3), then chatbot-widget.tsx:325, onboarding-wizard.tsx:161/177, ai-processing-banner.tsx:22/41, and the REC_COPY descriptions in src/lib/seo-geo.ts:949, 952, 953, 956, 958. Use `/usr/bin/grep -rn -- ' - ' 'src/app/(app)' src/components` (about 57 real copy hits out of 107 raw matches — the rest are arithmetic like `b.createdAt - a.createdAt`, skip those). Two traps: ai-processing-banner.tsx:22 will NOT appear in that grep because the hyphen opens a JSX text node, and do not touch the em-dash ban inside generated post text documented in docs/x-agent-portal.md.

title: One page, three different names: the staff sidebar says "Tasks", the client rail says "Workspace", the staff page header says "Task Board"
surface: /tasks and /clients/[id]/tasks (sidebar, client rail, page header, notification bell, dashboard card)
whatYouSee: A client's left rail item reads "Workspace" and the page it opens is titled "Workspace" — but their dashboard's attention card says "Open items on your task board" and the notification bell footer says "View task board". For staff the same route renders a header reading "Task Board" while their sidebar item says "Tasks", and once they pick a client it becomes "Workspace".
whyItsWrong: Four names for one destination. A client is pointed at their "task board" and no such label exists anywhere in their navigation. Staff click "Tasks", arrive at "Task Board", then at "Workspace". Nobody can build a stable mental model, and support conversations get ambiguous.
fix: Standardize on "Workspace". src/components/sidebar.tsx:35 — `label: "Tasks"` becomes `label: "Workspace"`. src/app/(app)/tasks/tasks-body.tsx:108 — `<PageHeader title="Task Board" />` becomes `<PageHeader title="Workspace" description="Every client's board in one place." />` (the scoped view at line 69-72 is already "Workspace"). src/components/notification-bell.tsx:264 — "View task board →" becomes "View workspace →". src/components/client-home-overview.tsx:99 — hint "Open items on your task board." becomes "Open items on your workspace board." Leave the copilot's internal prompt text (src/lib/ai/prompts/proactive-assistant.ts) and the chat route strings alone unless you also relabel the copilot chip.

title: The Activity tab's empty state promises clients "notes" that are filtered out of their view, and calls every agent run a "campaign"
whatYouSee: Empty state: "No activity yet — Events appear here as work is done: Intel Reports, campaigns, branding updates, and notes." Once populated, every agent run renders as "<Agent> campaign drafted" — including a single Reddit reply draft — and the research report row reads "Intel Report generated".
whyItsWrong: Two problems in one panel. Manual notes are stripped from the timeline for client accounts, so a client is told to expect the one thing they will never be shown, and "Intel Reports" is an internal product name that appears nowhere else in their portal. And "campaign" is used for every job, contradicting the "run", "deliverable" and "draft" vocabulary on every other client surface — one Reddit reply is not a campaign. The empty state also offers no next action.
fix: src/components/activity-timeline.tsx:374 — replace "Events appear here as work is done: Intel Reports, campaigns, branding updates, and notes." with "Every agent run, brand update, and competitor change shows up here as your team works." and, when `isStaff` is false (the flag already exists at line 342), add a link to `/clients/<clientId>/agents` labelled "Run an agent" — clientId is already a prop. Line 45 — replace `title: \`${j.agentName} campaign drafted\`` with `` `${j.agentName} delivered a draft` ``. Line 63 — replace "Intel Report generated" with "Research report ready". Do NOT bother editing EVENT_CONFIG.label (lines 101-161): those strings are never rendered.

title: Task cards are a single column of tall blocks — roughly two fit on screen
whatYouSee: The board renders one wide column of cards, each with a large empty lower half. At a normal window size about two cards are visible; the 14 pending items need continuous scrolling. Status is a word (“Pending”) rather than a column.
whyItsWrong: It is called a board but behaves as a list, so the one thing a board is for — seeing status distribution at a glance — is unavailable. The wasted vertical space inside each card is what pushes the count off screen.
fix: Give the card a fixed compact height (title, client chip, age, status dot) and lay the statuses out as real columns at wide widths, falling back to the current stacked list under the tablet breakpoint. Move the description behind hover or the ticket modal.

title: Nothing marks a post as posted, so the archive shows everything the moment it is generated
whatYouSee: Every generated deliverable appears in the archive immediately, badged "draft". The call decided the opposite flow: the calendar day card gets "Mark as posted"; the archive lists only what was actually posted (about the last 30 days); upcoming days show template slots without exposing pre-generated content — explicitly to avoid the churn risk of a client saying "just give me all the posts".
whyItsWrong: The schema already models it — assets have scheduled/approved/published states and the detail panel even asks "Already posted it?" — but the archive never filters on any of it. So the portal reveals the whole pre-generated batch, which is both the approval-promise break (finding 47) and the exact churn scenario the team named.
evidence: src/components/archive-view.tsx — no status filter on the client archive
asset-detail-modal — the "Already posted it?" control already writes the confirmation
Team decision, portal review call 27 Jul 2026
fix: Filter the client archive to posted content (status published, or the client's "Already posted it?" confirmation) and age it out after ~30 days; add "Mark as posted" to the calendar day card wired to the same status; keep drafts on the staff side only. Cross-ref finding 47 for the raw-markup half of the archive problem.

title: Video deliverables have no path into the portal — clips are hand-delivered by email
surface: Assets / Archive / Calendar — any video deliverable (podcast clips, branded shorts, TikTok)
whatYouSee: Podcast clips for a real client are delivered as a daily email from the Hello account because the portal cannot hold them; the produced clips live on a laptop. On the call: "It works — it's just we don't have the system to show the videos on the portal… we will use GCP block storage, and then the agent service could ask for the data."
whyItsWrong: Asset.kind has no video variant ("image" | "document" | "text" | "other"), the asset detail panel renders text and images only, and the single video player in the codebase is inside the task-ticket modal. Meanwhile three of the seven agents on the client's page (Branded Shorts, TikTok, Instagram clips lane) exist to produce video. The mimeType field already anticipates "video/mp4" for downloads — ingestion and playback are the missing halves.
evidence: src/components/task-ticket-modal.tsx:113 — the only <video> element in the app
src/lib/types.ts:388–396 — mimeType documents "video/mp4" for the download path only
Team decision, portal review call 27 Jul 2026: GCS block storage, agent service fetches from it
fix: Add kind "video" with a GCS-backed upload/URL field per the call decision; render a <video controls> player in the asset detail panel (lift the task-ticket player); show clips on calendar/archive like posts, with the existing copy-caption button beside them. Then the email workaround can retire.
